About
Media Buying Is Only Part of the Job
A quick look at how I think about performance marketing before the first ad ever goes live.

I'm a Performance Media Buyer with 2 years of experience working across 33 brands and multiple industries: fashion, footwear, hospitality, restaurants, cafés, bags, cosmetics, home & kitchen, gifts & accessories, sportswear, and more.

I manage performance campaigns with a business-first approach. I start by understanding the business and auditing its current performance before making decisions around products, pricing, unit economics, audience, and offers.

My work goes beyond media buying. I develop creative strategies and angles, build campaign structures, run tests, analyze performance data, optimize campaigns, and scale what works. I also work across tracking, analytics, pricing, and offer strategy to connect advertising performance with real business goals.

Across my experience, I have managed 6M+ EGP in ad spend, generating 45M+ EGP in revenue, with an 8X average ROAS.

The Challenge

The brand started from zero, with no existing product assets, photography, or video content. The client needed to validate product demand before committing to manufacturing, so the initial approach was built around a test-and-learn model from day one.

The initial objective was to identify which products had the strongest market potential using limited creative assets, then use those insights to guide product development and subsequent content production.

Main Goals
  • Achieve 8x ROAS
  • Maintain strong and consistent advertising performance
  • Validate products before manufacturing
Target Audience
  • Women aged 20–45
  • Interested in elegance and quality
  • Value-for-money mindset
What I Did

I started with a 3-day Traffic Campaign, followed by a Sales campaign.

Since there were no lifestyle or video assets available at the beginning, testing was conducted using isolated product images across the available products.

I structured the testing campaign by product category, creating 8 Ad Sets, each with an EGP 900 budget, to identify the products with the strongest demand.

Once the winning products were identified, the insights were shared with the client, allowing us to move into lifestyle shooting and Reels production from late January, ahead of the White Friday period.

Campaign & Creative Structure

The main formats used were:

  • Flexible Ads
  • Single Images & Videos
  • Advantage+ Catalog Ads with a strong introductory product
  • Carousel Ads using isolated product images

Isolated product images became one of the strongest-performing creative formats throughout the account.

I also created a dedicated Top Products CBO campaign, where winning creatives were continuously introduced, while underperforming creatives were excluded.

Retargeting

Retargeting campaigns were structured around different levels of user intent:

  • Website Visitors — 7, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, and 45 days
  • View Content & Add to Cart — same time-window structure
  • Engaged Users & Messages — same time-window structure
Testing, Optimization & Scaling

The strongest overall performance consistently came from Flexible Ads and isolated product images.

For prospecting, Advantage+ with broad targeting consistently outperformed the manual structures tested, including single and stacked audiences and single and stacked interests.

Ad Sets with consistently high CPP were turned off based on the predefined maximum acceptable CPP.

When a product performed well, I analyzed the creative responsible for the performance and used the insight to guide the next testing cycle:

  • For winning design creatives, I created new variations while maintaining the same successful angle.
  • For winning video creatives, I analyzed Hook Rate and Hold Rate, then tested the same creative approach across other products.
  • Winning creatives were also introduced into catalog campaigns to extend their performance.

For scaling, I used two approaches:

  • Vertical scaling by increasing the budget on winning Ad Sets.
  • Duplicating proven winners into dedicated scaling campaigns with higher budgets.

I also tested the same business through a second Ad Account after observing that algorithm behavior and performance could differ between accounts. The second account delivered better and more cost-efficient results, so it was used for scaling.

TikTok

On TikTok, I initially used manual campaigns with a high volume of creatives.

Winning creatives were then moved into Smart campaigns using 2x–3x the original campaign budget.

The structure focused on the combination of product + content, with strong-performing products separated into dedicated campaigns by category, such as Slippers and Flats.

Overall Outcome

Starting with no product assets and using paid media as a product-validation mechanism, the account evolved from initial isolated-product testing into a structured system covering creative testing, product validation, retargeting, catalog advertising, optimization, and scaling.

The approach ultimately generated over EGP 10.7M in gross revenue at a 10.13x ROAS.

📋 Key Performance Insight
High ROAS does not always mean that an Ad Set is contributing positively to the overall account performance. Some higher-cost Ad Sets could still contribute to warming audiences that eventually converted through other Ad Sets. Because of this, optimization was not based solely on individual Ad Set ROAS or CPP, but also on maintaining the overall performance of the advertising funnel and account.

TikTok Ads: Campaign Performance
TikTok Ads: Campaign Performance (Latest)
The Challenge

The brand operates in the premium and affordable luxury segment, with a strong and bold positioning. From the beginning, the advertising approach was built around a structured funnel rather than random creative production.

The challenge was to build demand around a wide range of summer products, including several designs that were unique to the brand and not widely available in the Egyptian market.

The initial stage focused on building awareness and demand before moving fully into purchase-driven campaigns. This included lead generation through forms, driving traffic to the website for product discovery, influencer activity, and video views across Meta and TikTok.

What I Did

I built the creative and campaign structure around clear concepts, angles, and funnel stages, rather than treating every creative as an isolated ad.

The initial testing structure included:

  • Influencers & UGC
  • Studio Reels
  • Designs
  • White-background carousels
  • Catalog campaigns
  • Instagram followers & Page Likes
  • Video Views for brand exposure

One of the strongest findings from testing was the performance of isolated white-background creatives.

These creatives performed strongly because they clearly showcased the products and allowed users to see the details of each design.

We also identified one influencer who generated significantly stronger sales than the other three tested. The winning influencer creatives were moved into a dedicated campaign, with the budget increased by 3x, while some winning creatives were also duplicated for further testing and scaling.

For creatives that did not perform well with broad targeting, I shifted toward stacked interest audiences to test whether more specific audience signals could improve performance.

Data-Driven Optimization

I broke down the available performance data to identify patterns in purchasing behavior.

The analysis showed that the strongest purchasing period was between 12 PM to 6 PM, with strong sales coming from:

  • New Cairo
  • Sheikh Zayed
  • Alexandria

Based on these insights, winning creatives were focused on these locations and time periods, which generated strong sales performance.

Another recurring challenge was the performance of specific shoe sizes. When certain sizes were not selling effectively, I created dedicated Special Sizes creatives and supported them with Flash Sale offers to help move the remaining inventory.

Offer & Inventory Strategy

During the final stage of the Summer Collection, the business needed to convert existing inventory into cash and avoid keeping stock in the warehouse while preparing for the Winter Collection.

After calculating the business costs, we introduced a Buy 1 Get 1 offer.

I created static creatives communicating the offer and adapted previously successful creative concepts by integrating the new offer into their messaging.

At this stage, the objective was not to maximize profit margin. The priority was to liquidate the existing inventory without taking a loss, generate cash flow, and prepare for the upcoming Winter Collection.

The maximum acceptable CPP was set at EGP 350 based on this objective.

WhatsApp Retargeting

To reduce advertising costs and make better use of the existing customer base, I used WhatsApp to communicate the offer directly to previous customers who had already purchased from the brand.

This allowed us to retarget existing customers without relying entirely on paid advertising, while keeping the cost of re-engagement lower.

Meta Scaling Approach

The Meta campaigns were scaled using a dynamic push-and-pull approach.

For example:

  • Campaign budget starts at EGP 2,000
  • If performance remained strong after approximately two hours, the budget was increased to EGP 4,000
  • At the end of the day, the budget was returned to its original level to avoid disrupting campaign performance

This approach allowed us to push spend during strong performance windows while maintaining the original campaign structure.

TikTok Strategy

On TikTok, the strongest-performing approach was Smart Campaigns.

The process started with a clear creative direction based on the target persona and audience, followed by producing a high volume of creatives — sometimes reaching 25–30 videos across:

  • UGC
  • Influencers
  • Lifestyle
  • Studio Reels

Underperforming creatives were turned off quickly to give stronger creatives more room to receive spend and generate performance.

For winning creatives, I tested different bid levels around the target cost:

  • One Ad Set at approximately 20% above the target cost
  • Another at approximately 20% below the target cost

The winning setup was then scaled using the same approach, while creatives that failed to perform were continuously removed.

📋 Overall Approach
The account was managed through a combination of structured creative testing, funnel-based thinking, audience analysis, inventory-led offers, and performance-based scaling. Rather than treating creative production and media buying as separate activities, campaign decisions were continuously connected to product performance, audience behavior, inventory needs, and business objectives. Current performance period is ongoing.

The Challenge

ChocoBom introduced a unique product to the Egyptian market by combining traditional Turkish coffee with milk and cocoa into a single ready-to-prepare beverage.

Since this product category was relatively new, the primary challenge wasn't simply generating sales—it was educating the market, building trust, and encouraging customers to try a completely new coffee experience.

The objective was to build strong brand awareness, create social proof around the product, and develop a scalable acquisition strategy capable of converting first-time buyers into repeat customers.

Marketing Strategy

The marketing strategy focused on making customers experience the product before asking them to purchase it.

Rather than relying on traditional product advertising, the communication centered around authentic experiences, emotional reactions, and social proof to introduce ChocoBom as a new way to enjoy Turkish coffee.

To encourage trial and increase purchase intent, campaigns combined educational content, influencer marketing, promotional offers, and value-driven product bundles.

Creative Strategy

Since the product was unfamiliar to most consumers, content became the primary growth driver.

The creative mix included:

  • UGC videos featuring real people trying ChocoBom for the first time.
  • Influencer collaborations sharing honest product reviews and tasting experiences.
  • Lifestyle videos showcasing different consumption occasions such as breakfast, work, and evening coffee breaks.
  • Promotional designs highlighting seasonal offers, bundles, and free gifts.
  • Product-focused videos demonstrating preparation and explaining the product's unique benefits.

Alongside paid advertising, the brand also invested heavily in organic social media content to continuously build credibility and maintain a strong social presence.

Creative Insights

Throughout the testing phase, authentic content consistently outperformed traditional promotional creatives.

UGC videos generated the strongest engagement because they allowed potential customers to experience genuine first reactions before making a purchase.

Influencer collaborations played a major role in building credibility for a completely new product category, helping reduce hesitation and encouraging customers to give the product a try.

Lifestyle videos successfully positioned ChocoBom as part of customers' everyday routines rather than simply another coffee product.

Offer-based creatives achieved the highest conversion rates during scaling phases, particularly when combined with bundle offers and free gifts, increasing both purchase volume and Average Order Value.

These insights became the foundation for future content production and budget allocation throughout the account.

Offer Strategy

Rather than competing through discounts alone, the promotional strategy focused on increasing the perceived value of every purchase.

Multiple bundle combinations were tested throughout the campaign, including offers with free gifts and free shipping, encouraging customers to purchase multiple boxes instead of a single product.

This approach increased the Average Order Value while maintaining healthy profitability and created stronger incentives for first-time customers to try the product.

The offer strategy became one of the account's strongest scaling levers, especially during seasonal campaigns and promotional periods.

Campaign Structure & Testing Framework

The account was structured around continuous creative testing and product education.

Different creative formats, messaging angles, promotional offers, and bundles were tested simultaneously to identify the combinations that generated the strongest purchase intent.

Performance analysis focused on:

  • Creative performance.
  • Product education effectiveness.
  • Customer acquisition cost.
  • Purchase conversion.
  • Average Order Value (AOV).
  • Return on Ad Spend (ROAS).

Winning creatives were continuously refreshed while maintaining successful messaging to minimize creative fatigue and sustain long-term performance.

Scaling Strategy

Once high-performing creatives, offers, and bundles were identified, budget allocation shifted toward proven combinations.

Scaling focused on:

  • Increasing budgets behind winning creatives.
  • Producing additional variations using the same successful creative angles.
  • Expanding bundle offers that increased Average Order Value.
  • Leveraging additional UGC creators and influencer collaborations to continuously generate fresh social proof.

This allowed the account to scale efficiently while maintaining acquisition performance throughout the year.

Tracking & Analytics

Performance and business decisions were supported through:

  • Shopify Reports for sales analysis, inventory management, and product performance.
  • Looker Studio for centralized dashboards and business reporting.
  • Google Analytics 4 (GA4) to analyze customer acquisition, user behavior, and conversion paths.
  • Microsoft Clarity for session recordings, heatmaps, and customer journey analysis.
  • Claude AI, connected through the Meta Marketing API, to automate reporting, accelerate campaign analysis, and streamline optimization workflows.
📋 Key Learning
Managing ChocoBom reinforced the importance of education and trust when introducing a new product category. Customers were not simply deciding whether to buy coffee—they first needed to understand what the product was, how it tasted, and why it was different from traditional Turkish coffee. Building social proof through UGC creators and influencers proved significantly more effective than relying on conventional product advertisements alone. Combined with value-driven bundle offers and continuous creative testing, this approach enabled the brand to grow efficiently while establishing strong credibility within a competitive food and beverage market.

The Challenge

Ease by Rana Sallam initially built its customer base through organic social media and direct messages before launching its e-commerce website in May 2025.

The objective was to transition the brand into a scalable e-commerce business powered by Meta Ads while maintaining profitability during the peak burkini season. Before investing heavily in paid acquisition, the focus was placed on creating a seamless customer journey and building a testing framework that would identify the most effective products, creatives, and growth opportunities.

Website & Customer Journey Optimization

Before launching paid campaigns, I focused on optimizing the website to remove friction throughout the purchasing journey and improve conversion rates.

The website was reviewed from both a user experience and conversion optimization perspective to ensure customers could confidently complete their purchases.

Key improvements included:

  • Optimizing product pages to reduce purchase hesitation.
  • Improving the visibility and accessibility of the Size Guide.
  • Adding a custom sizing option that allowed customers to submit their height and weight for personalized size recommendations.
  • Introducing an additional checkout incentive by offering an extra discount when customers completed their purchase.
  • Implementing product recommendations to cross-sell matching cardigans alongside the selected burkini.

These improvements significantly strengthened the purchase funnel, increasing the Add to Cart → Checkout conversion rate from approximately 24% to 48%.

Creative Strategy

As the brand was entering paid advertising for the first time, the initial objective was to identify both the highest-performing products and the creative formats capable of generating scalable results.

The creative strategy included multiple content formats designed to test different customer motivations:

  • Promotional design creatives highlighting the Launch Offer.
  • Lifestyle videos filmed at the beach to showcase the product in its natural environment.
  • Storytelling videos presented by the brand owner to communicate the brand's vision and build trust.
  • UGC (User-Generated Content) focused on authentic customer experiences and product reviews.

This diversified creative approach allowed continuous testing across different content styles while collecting actionable performance data.

Creative Insights

Throughout the testing phase, I continuously analyzed creative performance to understand which content formats influenced customer behavior across different stages of the funnel.

Lifestyle videos consistently generated the strongest engagement and helped customers visualize the product in real-life beach settings, making them highly effective for attracting qualified traffic.

UGC videos played an important role in building trust by addressing common customer concerns around sizing, comfort, fit, and fabric quality. These creatives significantly improved purchase confidence, particularly among first-time buyers.

Storytelling videos presented by the brand owner strengthened the emotional connection with the audience by communicating the brand's mission, values, and attention to quality. This format helped humanize the brand and reinforce credibility.

Promotional design creatives performed particularly well during the launch period by clearly communicating the limited-time launch offer and creating urgency. Once winning promotional angles were identified, new creative variations were produced while maintaining the same messaging to maximize performance and minimize creative fatigue.

These insights directly influenced both future content production and budget allocation, allowing investment to be concentrated on the creative formats that consistently generated the strongest business results.

Campaign Structure & Testing Framework

The account was structured around creative testing rather than audience complexity during the initial launch phase.

Testing campaigns were segmented by content format, allowing each creative type to be evaluated independently before scaling.

The primary goals during testing were to identify:

  • Winning products.
  • The highest-performing creative formats.
  • The strongest creative angles.
  • Customer behavior throughout the purchase journey.
  • Opportunities to improve conversion performance.

Instead of optimizing solely for ROAS, I continuously analyzed the full customer journey to understand where users were dropping off and what improvements could unlock additional revenue.

Funnel Optimization

One of the biggest challenges identified during the testing phase was the significant drop-off between Add to Cart and Checkout.

Although Add to Cart rates were healthy, a relatively small percentage of users continued to the checkout stage.

To address this issue, I optimized the product page experience by improving information clarity, strengthening customer confidence, and reducing uncertainty during the buying decision.

The combination of personalized sizing assistance, improved product information, stronger product presentation, additional checkout incentives, and relevant cross-selling recommendations successfully doubled the Add to Cart → Checkout conversion rate from 24% to 48%, creating a significantly healthier purchase funnel.

Scaling Strategy

Once winning products and creative formats were identified, budget allocation shifted toward proven performers.

Scaling focused on increasing investment behind the highest-performing products while continuously producing new creative variations based on winning angles and messaging.

This approach allowed the account to maintain performance throughout the season while reducing creative fatigue and maximizing return on ad spend.

Tracking & Analytics

Performance analysis and business decisions were supported through:

  • Shopify Reports for sales, inventory, and product performance analysis.
  • Looker Studio for centralized performance dashboards and business reporting.
  • Google Analytics 4 (GA4) to analyze customer acquisition, user behavior, and conversion paths.
  • Microsoft Clarity for session recordings, heatmaps, and customer journey analysis.
  • Claude AI, connected through the Meta Marketing API, to automate repetitive analysis tasks and accelerate campaign optimization workflows.
📋 Key Learning
While the business benefited from the seasonal demand for burkinis, the growth was driven by a structured testing framework, continuous funnel optimization, and a data-driven creative strategy that identified the products and content formats capable of scaling profitably.

The Challenge

Buying bridal shoes is a highly emotional decision, unlike ordinary footwear purchases. Brides typically begin planning months in advance and hesitate to buy online due to concerns about comfort, sizing, quality, and whether the shoes will be perfect for one of the most important days of their lives. The primary objective was not only to drive sales, but to build trust and reduce purchase anxiety throughout the customer journey.

What I Did

Instead of positioning purely around "bridal," I built the strategy around customer intent and occasion: brides, engagement ceremonies, contract-signing ceremonies, graduations, bridesmaids, and mothers/sisters of the bride. This expanded the addressable audience while keeping messaging relevant to each segment. For brides specifically, communication emphasized reassurance, comfort, and confidence over discounts or product specs.

  • Lifestyle videos in real wedding settings, the highest engagement, helped brides visualize wearing the shoes.
  • Voice-over videos directly addressing comfort, quality, and confidence concerns, the most effective at reducing hesitation.
  • Static designs for seasonal launches and collections, best during promotional periods.
  • Organic and paid content worked as one consistent brand experience rather than two separate channels.
Results Over Time

The account experienced a temporary pause between the peak of one season and the start of the next before advertising resumed. Following the relaunch, continued creative and audience refinement pushed ROAS from 7.65x to 8.6x, reflecting ongoing optimization of creative strategy, audience quality, and campaign structure, while maintaining a strong focus on customer trust throughout the purchasing journey.

📋 Key Learning
Widening the occasion, not the product, grew the addressable market without diluting the message. Brides still received a dedicated, trust-first message while the same catalog reached engagements, graduations, and bridesmaids.

The Challenge

This brand entered the market as a new e-commerce label specializing in premium home textiles and bedding: mattress toppers, bed sheets, duvet sets, mattress protectors, and towels. Since the brand was newly launched, the challenge wasn't only generating sales, it was establishing credibility, building customer trust, and creating demand with a limited marketing budget.

Launch Strategy

During the early launch phase, budget efficiency was the top priority. Instead of investing heavily in expensive production, I used AI-generated product designs to quickly produce high-quality creatives at low cost, enabling the brand to start advertising immediately, validate market demand, and generate profitable sales without a large creative budget. As the account scaled, the creative strategy gradually shifted toward more lifestyle-focused content.

Website & Creative Evolution

Website optimization ran continuously alongside campaign work rather than as a one-time task. Customer behavior was regularly analyzed to identify friction points and refine navigation, product presentation, and purchase flow.

Lifestyle videos demonstrating products in realistic bedroom environments consistently outperformed static creatives by helping customers visualize the product at home. Offer-based creatives generated the strongest intent during promotional periods by increasing perceived value rather than relying solely on discounts.

📋 Key Learning
A limited launch budget isn't a blocker, it's a constraint that forces the right sequencing: validate cheap and fast first with AI-assisted creative, then reinvest in production once demand is proven.

The Challenge

Pukka's social media presence lacked a clear marketing direction. Content was being published inconsistently, while advertising creatives were not structured around defined creative angles or funnel stages.

The website also lacked a clear product structure and several elements were affecting the overall shopping experience and website speed.

Website Rebuild, First

I started by improving the website structure and customer experience, including:

  • Reorganized the Winter Collection into Half Boots, Ankle Boots, and Long Boots.
  • Optimized the announcement bar, hamburger menu, and hero banner.
  • Removed unnecessary Shopify applications that were affecting website speed.
  • Made product variants and offers clearly visible across collection and homepage sections.
  • Improved the visibility and presentation of the size chart.
  • Updated the website policies and FAQs.
  • Made the website available in both Arabic and English.
  • Ensured the brand's social media channels were properly connected and accessible through the website.
Inventory-Led Content Strategy

After the website improvements, I shifted the focus to inventory and product performance.

I analyzed which products were selling and which were not, then built the content strategy around available inventory:

  • High-performing products with available stock: Increased creative production and developed multiple angles to support scaling.
  • Low-performing products with available stock: Used stronger offers to help move inventory.
  • Mid-performing products: Tested multiple approaches, including catalog campaigns, different creatives, and UGC content to build product trust and improve sales.

I also created a structured creative sheet containing the creative angles, concepts, references, products, and content formats — including designs, UGC, lifestyle content, and studio reels — to organize the testing process and allocate budgets based on the available creative assets.

Campaign & Testing Structure

I built a product-based testing campaign, organizing products according to their available inventory and the content created for each one.

I also structured catalog campaigns into four groups:

  • All Products
  • Long Boots
  • Half Boots
  • Ankle Boots

Additionally, I ran an Instagram follower campaign while excluding previous purchasers to focus on acquiring new audiences.

During the initial testing phase, I used higher testing budgets, starting from EGP 1,000 per ad set, due to the client's need to generate performance signals quickly.

Once a product performed well, I analyzed which creative was driving the result:

  • For winning design creatives, I developed new variations while maintaining the same winning angle.
  • For winning video creatives, I analyzed the Hook Rate and Hold Rate, then tested the same creative approach on other products.
  • Winning creatives were also introduced into collection catalog campaigns to extend their performance.
Scaling Approach

For winning creatives, I used two main scaling approaches:

  1. Vertical scaling by increasing the budget.
  2. Moving winning creatives into dedicated scaling campaigns with larger budgets focused on proven performers.

This allowed the scaling process to remain centered around creatives and products that had already demonstrated performance.

Results & Business Impact

A major challenge throughout the period was product quality and the resulting return rate. Imported products generally performed better and generated fewer returns, while locally sourced products experienced significantly higher returns, which limited the ability to fully capitalize on the generated sales.

For the Summer Collection, the approach was adjusted. Instead of committing to large inventory quantities upfront, the focus was placed on identifying which products had stronger market demand first, then allocating more content production and restocking around those products.

The return challenge continued due to the delivery offices the owner was working with, but the client was satisfied with the profitability achieved during this period.

Tracking & Analytics

Performance and business decisions were supported through:

  • Shopify Reports for sales and inventory analysis.
  • Looker Studio, connected via API, for continuous inventory and performance analysis.
  • GA4 to analyze the customer journey and understand acquisition performance across new and returning users.
📋 Key Learning
Top-line ROAS doesn't tell the whole story: imported products consistently returned less and performed better than locally sourced ones, which limited how much of the generated sales could actually be capitalized on. Adjusting the Summer Collection to validate demand before committing to inventory helped protect profitability despite an ongoing returns challenge.
